t:
That the portion of section 3(b) of the National Capital Transportation Act of 1965 (40 U.S.C. 682) which precedes paragraph (1) is amended to read as follows:


“(b) 
The work authorized by this section shall be subject to the provisions of the National Capital Transportation Act of 1960, shall be carried out substantially in accordance with the plans and schedules contained in the aforesaid report, as modified in the report of the Agency entitled ‘Revised Transit Development Program for the Nation’s Capital, 1967’, and shall be subject to the following:”.

fable.w: This section only amends the introductory text of an existing provision so that authorized transit work follows the plans and schedules in a federal agency's report, as modified by a later Agency report. The tempting reading is that references to "plans" and a "report of the Agency" imply some consultative process, but the Agency is a federal entity and nothing here calls for comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or consultation with any outside party. No non-federal actor is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be carried out substantially in accordance with the plans and schedules contained in the aforesaid report

qwen_block.w: This section mandates that work be carried out in accordance with specific plans and schedules contained in reports. It does not establish a process for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with the government, comment on decisions, or participate in advisory bodies. The reference to 'the Agency' and 'the report' indicates internal government planning and execution, not external participation.
qwen_block.s: The work authorized by this section shall be subject to the provisions of the National Capital Transportation Act of 1960, shall be carried out substantially in accordance with the plans and schedules contained in the aforesaid report, as modified in the report of the Agency entitled ‘Revised Transit Development Program for the Nation’s Capital, 1967’, and shall be subject to the following:

opus.w: This amendment only requires the transit work to follow existing plans and a revised agency report, and to be subject to an earlier Act. No party outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to object or sue. Referring to another statute or to the conditions that follow does not, on its own, create any participation by outsiders in a federal decision.
opus.s: shall be carried out substantially in accordance with the plans and schedules contained in the aforesaid report, as modified in the report of the Agency entitled ‘Revised Transit Development Program for the Nation’s Capital, 1967’
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section makes the work "subject to the provisions of the National Capital Transportation Act of 1960" and ties it to an agency report. Someone might guess that the 1960 Act or the conditions that follow involve consultation with local governments or the public. But the section itself names no outside party, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. It only says the work must follow existing plans and a revised agency report. Agency reports and plans stay inside the federal government, and a cross-reference alone does not show any participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates that work be carried out in accordance with existing plans and reports. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The reference to 'plans and schedules' is a directive to follow pre-existing documents, not a requirement for a participatory process like a hearing, comment period, or advisory committee. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The work authorized by this section shall be subject to the provisions of the National Capital Transportation Act of 1960, shall be carried out substantially in accordance with the plans and schedules contained in the aforesaid report, as modified in the report of the Agency entitled ‘Revised Transit Development Program for the Nation’s Capital, 1967’, and shall be subject to the following:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "plans and schedules contained in the aforesaid report" implies a prior process of public input or consultation that generated those plans. However, the text itself does not mandate any participation; it merely references existing documents. Furthermore, the section is purely administrative, defining the scope of work based on prior reports. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders *before* making the decision to carry out the work in this specific section; it just says the work must follow the plans. The "aforesaid report" is a static reference, not an active participation mechanism described in this text.
